spots.title: The face
spots.text: A bearded man with long hair, eyes closed. The face looks swollen on the right cheek and nose, which pathologists read as blows. On the cloth it is faint and hard to read. Switch to Negative and it becomes a portrait.
spots.verse: They spat on him, and took the reed and struck him on the head.

spots.title: Puncture wounds on the forehead
spots.text: Small blood flows on the forehead and in the hair, including one shaped like a reversed number 3. They match sharp objects pressed into the scalp, such as a cap of thorns.
spots.verse: The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.
spots.skeptic: A crown of thorns is a Gospel detail any artist would include.

spots.title: The nail wound in the wrist
spots.text: The hands are crossed over the groin. The visible wound is at the wrist, not the palm, where medieval art almost always placed it. Experiments by surgeon Pierre Barbet in the 1930s suggested nails through the palms cannot hold a body's weight.
spots.verse: Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.
spots.skeptic: Pathologists disagree on the exact path of the nail. Later pathologists, such as Frederick Zugibe, disputed Barbet's claim that palm nails cannot hold a body.

spots.title: No thumbs visible
spots.text: Only four fingers show on each hand. Barbet proposed that a nail through the wrist damages the median nerve and pulls the thumb into the palm.
spots.skeptic: Two incompatible medical explanations exist, and an artist could simply have hidden the thumbs.

spots.title: Blood running down the forearms
spots.text: Thin rivulets run from the wrists toward the elbows at angles that fit arms raised above the head, as on a cross.
spots.verse: where they crucified him, and with him two others, on either side one, and Jesus in the middle.
spots.skeptic: A 2018 bloodstain study by Borrini and Garlaschelli argued these flows need different arm positions.

spots.title: The wound in the side
spots.text: A large blood stain on the man's right side, below an oval wound about 4.5 cm across between the ribs. Lighter zones within it have been read as blood mixed with clear fluid, as John describes.
spots.verse: However, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
spots.skeptic: The "water" is an interpretation of lighter areas in the stain.

spots.title: Scourge marks on the legs
spots.text: Small dumbbell-shaped marks continue on the front of the thighs and calves, the same shape as on the back.
spots.verse: So Pilate then took Jesus and flogged him.

spots.title: Puncture wounds on the back of the head
spots.text: Blood flows cover the back of the head, more like a cap of thorns than the neat ring painted in art.
spots.verse: The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.

spots.title: Abraded shoulders
spots.text: Broad, scuffed areas over the shoulder blades, read by pathologists as pressure from carrying a heavy beam.
spots.verse: He went out, bearing his cross, to the place called “The Place of a Skull”, which is called in Hebrew, “Golgotha”,
spots.skeptic: These areas are faint and their reading depends on what you expect to see.

spots.title: More than 100 scourge marks
spots.text: Paired, dumbbell-shaped marks from the shoulders to the calves, in fan-shaped groups, as if from two men on either side. They match the lead weights of a Roman flagrum.
spots.verse: So Pilate then took Jesus and flogged him.
spots.skeptic: Counts come from enhanced photographs and vary from one author to another.

spots.title: A band of blood across the lower back
spots.text: A horizontal flow across the small of the back, often explained as blood from the side wound running around the body when it was laid down.
spots.verse: However, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
spots.skeptic: Borrini and Garlaschelli judged this band unrealistic.

spots.title: The sole of the foot
spots.text: A clear imprint of the right sole with a blood stain at the center, where a nail through the feet would exit.
spots.verse: See my hands and my feet, that it is truly me. Touch me and see, for a spirit doesn’t have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.

spots.title: The 1532 fire
spots.text: On 4 December 1532 the cloth, folded in a silver case in the chapel of the castle at Chambéry, then capital of the Duchy of Savoy, was nearly destroyed by fire. Molten silver burned through the folds, leaving these symmetric lines of scorches and holes along both sides.

spots.title: The patches of the Poor Clares
spots.text: In 1534 Poor Clare nuns in Chambéry sewed triangular patches over the burn holes and backed the cloth with a support cloth. The patches were removed in a 2002 restoration. This 1931 photograph shows them.

spots.title: Water stains
spots.text: Large diamond-shaped stains repeat along the cloth. Long thought to come from water thrown on the 1532 fire, a 2002 study proposed, as a hypothesis, that some are older, from the cloth being folded and stored in a jar.

spots.title: The "poker holes"
spots.text: Four sets of small burn holes in an L-shaped pattern, older than the 1532 fire. They appear in a painted copy of 1516. Some researchers see the same pattern in a Hungarian manuscript from about 1192, the Pray Codex.
spots.skeptic: Whether the Pray Codex drawing shows these holes is disputed.

spots.title: The side strip
spots.text: A strip about 8 cm wide runs along one whole edge, joined by a seam. Swiss textile expert Mechthild Flury-Lemberg compared the seam to one on first-century fabric from Masada.
spots.skeptic: Seams like this are not unique to the first century, and the comparison remains disputed.

spots.title: Where the carbon dating sample was cut
spots.text: In 1988 a single strip was cut near this corner, at the feet end of the front image, and divided among three laboratories. Approximate location; the 1931 photograph predates the sampling.
